newsitem.title: UK: Shell Chem sells MMA process to ICI.
newsitem.headline: Shell Chem sells MMA process to ICI.

text.p: Shell International Chemicals Ltd, part of the Anglo-Dutch Royal Dutch Shell Group, said on Friday it had sold its novel chemical process for producing MMA and other methacrylate monomers to ICI Acrylics, part of British-based chemicals giant ICI Plc.

"The outright sale of a technology which Shell has not commercialised is a novel approach and reflects the drive to focus its activities only in business areas where it can achieve a world leadership position," Shell said in a statement.
It gave no financial details on the transaction.
The process, which uses petrochemical cracker feedstocks, was invented in the late 1980s as part of studies into applications for synthesis gas and carbon monoxide, Shell added.

While those studies have led to some other developments which have been commercialised by Shell, in the case of MMA the company said it had decided "it is unable rapidly to generate a core business from its current position".

"In the hands of ICI Acrylics this elegant chemistry can be developed into a highly competitive production process and the sale of the technology represents a good return on the reseach and development investment," it added.
